description: Hybrid approaches combine classical tree-based force approximation with learned corrections. A neural network can learn the residual error between a low-order multipole approximation and the true force, achieving high accuracy with fewer multipole terms. This bridges the efficiency of FMM/Barnes-Hut with the expressiveness of neural networks.
mathematical_formalization: F_hybrid(i) = F_multipole(i, p=1) + F_neural(h_i, context_i), where F_multipole uses low-order Barnes-Hut approximation and F_neural is a learned correction. Loss: |F_hybrid - F_direct|^2.
analogical_connections: Residual learning (ResNets): learning correction to identity is easier than learning the full mapping
Kalman filtering: physics-based prediction + data-driven update
Hybrid vehicles: mechanical engine provides base power, electric motor provides correction
implementation_hypothesis: Run Barnes-Hut with theta=1.0 (fast but inaccurate). Train MLP to predict force residual given particle position, local density, and the Barnes-Hut estimate itself.
experiment_seed: Train hybrid on N=1000 particles. Test on N=5000. Compare direct summation, Barnes-Hut theta=0.5, and hybrid accuracy and speed.
